data.headline: Semiconductor Earnings Are Coming. 1 Stock to Buy, According to an Analyst.
data.summary: Semiconductor earnings are just around the corner, and Citi says that challenged personal computer and auto markets will dent results for some companies.  Citi analyst Christopher Danely says he expects chip companies’ financial result to be worse than Wall Street’s consensus estimates.  Weak demand in the PC and auto markets, as well as excess inventory, could drag down the  index (ticker: SOX) for a tumble, he wrote in a Wednesday note.

data.headline: Qualcomm to wait until after election to possibly buy Intel: BBG
data.summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) may wait until after the 2024 US presidential election in three weeks to decide whether or not to buy chipmaker Intel (INTC), according to Bloomberg reports. Morning Brief hosts Seana Smith and Brad Smith report more on this news as the tech company weighs potential anti-trust pushback from the administration elected in November and the state of the United States' relationship with China. data.headline: Is the Nvidia stock sell-off done?
data.summary: Nvidia (NVDA) shares have retreated from its record high. The sell-off was triggered by the surprise rout in chip player ASML (ASML), which shocked investors this week by offering a weak outlook. The company cited softening demand for non-AI applications. But drilling deeper, all indications are that demand for Nvidia’s new Blackwell chip remains very robust. So is the sell-off overdone in the market’s most popular stock? On today's Opening Bid Market Minute, host Brian Sozzi explores why this sector-wide sell-off might not accurately reflect Nvidia's robust fundamentals.
